## Fig 12 — Political parties (an extension, not in the paper)
[`fig12_political_parties.png`](fig12_political_parties.png). Code in `herding/politics.py`; the
numbers below come from `python3 scripts/analysis/president_party_gap.py`. The president's party is taken from inauguration
dates (12 changes of party from 1928 to 2026). The "presidential puzzle" (Santa-Clara &
Valkanov 2003; Pástor & Veronesi 2020) says US stocks return more under Democratic presidents,
with no matching difference in risk.

The 1928 file has 11 wrong closes (a 3–10% "move" undone the next day while the Dow barely
moved, e.g. 1935-04-16: S&P −10.0%, Dow +0.4%). They were found by checking every day from 1928
to 1952 against the Dow Jones average (MeasuringWorth) and are left out when the data is loaded
(`market_data.BAD_CLOSES`, November 2026). The numbers below are from after that fix.

The model has no politics in it, so it can serve as a yardstick for luck. Every gap is
measured in units of the series' own daily sd, so that markets of different volatility can be
compared. Two yardsticks:
- **the model:** 40 S&P-calibrated histories, cut at the real inauguration dates;
- **the real returns with the party calendar slid along:** whole quarters, at least a year away
  from the real calendar (386 fake calendars for 1928–, 299 for 1950–). This keeps the market's own
  calm and wild spells.

| S&P 500 | 1928–2026 | 1950–2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Return gap, Democrats − Republicans | **+6.8% a year** | +5.3% a year |
| ... percentile among shifted calendars / model | **97% / 100%** | 95% / 100% |
| Volatility D ÷ R | 0.87 (26% / 10%) | 0.86 (13% / 10%) |
| Fat tails (kurtosis) D − R | −11.2 (20% / 10%) | −28 (13% / 0%) |
| Crash days (below −4 sd) per 1,000, D − R | −2.2 (30% / 15%) | −1.6 (27% / 22%) |

- **The return gap is real but borderline.** Against the fair yardstick (shifted calendars) it
  sits at the 95th–97th percentile. With only 12 changes of party, a few eras carry much of it:
  leaving out the years 1929–1932 (the crash, under Hoover) shrinks it to 3.7% a year (leaving out
  exactly Hoover's term, March 1929 to March 1933: 3.1%), and leaving out 2008 (Bush) as well
  shrinks it to 2.4%.
- **The model is the wrong yardstick for average returns.** Its returns reverse from day to day
  (H 0.39, the miss in Fig 7), so its long-run averages wobble too little, and every real gap
  looks extreme against it. For volatility, tails and crashes the two yardsticks agree on the
  S&P, but the model's yardstick is too narrow for those as well (see "Is the luck test itself
  sound?" below), so the shifted calendar is the one to trust.
- **No party difference in crashes, volatility or fat tails.** Every one sits inside both
  yardsticks. The −28 kurtosis gap since 1950 is mostly one day: without Black Monday 1987 (under a
  Republican president) it is −8.3.
- **What this means for the project question:** the crash-making mechanism (herding) shows no
  sign of depending on the party in power. Parties may shift average returns, as Pástor &
  Veronesi argue, through investors' fear, which this model does not have. Party is correlation,
  not cause: this test cannot say what drives the gap.

## Fig 12b — Term by term: which presidencies can the model explain? (extension)

## Fig 13–15 — Parties at scale: 130 years, 24 markets (extension, November 2026)

Code: `python3 scripts/party_figures.py` (the three figures), `python3 scripts/analysis/party_scale.py`
(the numbers; about 3 minutes), tests in `tests/test_party_figures.py`, `tests/test_party_scale.py`
and `tests/test_politics_heavy.py`. Fig 12 used the S&P since 1928 and 40 model histories. Here
the test is run on the **Dow Jones average since 1896** (35,247 trading days, 15 changes of
party; from MeasuringWorth), the S&P, the Nasdaq-100 and the 20 stocks, against **1,000** model
histories (seeds 60000–60999; 20 ran away and were left out).

- [`fig13_parties_130_years.png`](fig13_parties_130_years.png): $1 in the Dow in 1896 became
  $1,639 by 2026 (price only: no dividends, no inflation). Invested only under Democratic
  presidents it became $106; only under Republican presidents, $15. But without Clinton the
  Democratic $1 ends at $33, and without Hoover the Republican $1 ends at $91.
- [`fig14_every_presidency.png`](fig14_every_presidency.png): every presidency since 1896 side by
  side. Best yearly return: Coolidge (R, +26%); worst: Hoover (R, −36%). Wildest: Hoover;
  calmest: Johnson (D). Both parties have rows at both ends.
- [`fig15_is_the_gap_luck.png`](fig15_is_the_gap_luck.png): the real gap against every shifted
  party calendar, and the gap in every 40-year window of the Dow: from −4.2% to +13.9% a year,
  and negative (better under Republicans) for windows ending about 1975–1995.

| Market | Years | Party changes | Gap D − R a year | 95% range (bootstrap) | Beats % of shifted calendars |

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ caches follow the files they read
# Spec: a cached value that comes from a file is read again when that file changes (its time is part
# of the cache key), and the site's reload list covers every herding module the pages load.

def test_file_stamp_and_data_stamp(tmp_path):
    import os
    from web import common as c
    a, missing = tmp_path / "a.json", tmp_path / "nope.json"
    a.write_text("{}")
    os.utime(a, (1_000_000.0, 1_000_000.0))
    assert c.file_stamp(a, missing) == (1_000_000.0, 0.0)
    os.utime(a, (1_000_060.0, 1_000_060.0))
    assert c.file_stamp(a) == (1_000_060.0,)
    newest = max(p.stat().st_mtime for p in c.DATA.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
    assert c.data_stamp() == newest


@pytest.mark.parametrize("public, private, path_attr", [
    ("fitted", "_fitted", "FIT"),
])
def test_fit_is_read_again_when_the_settings_file_changes(monkeypatch, public, private, path_attr):
    import os
    import streamlit as st
    from herding import explore as ex
    from web import common as c
    st.cache_data.clear()
    calls = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(ex, "fitted_settings", lambda: calls.append(1) or ({"n": len(calls)}, 1000))
    path = getattr(ex, path_attr)
    before = os.stat(path)
    try:
        assert getattr(c, public)()[0] == {"n": 1} and getattr(c, public)()[0] == {"n": 1}
        os.utime(path, (before.st_atime, before.st_mtime + 60))       # what a refit + push does
        assert getattr(c, public)()[0] == {"n": 2}
    finally:
        os.utime(path, (before.st_atime, before.st_mtime))
        st.cache_data.clear()

    # run_mixes was cached on (a1, a2, v1, days, seed) only: after a refit it kept serving runs made

    import os

        assert c.run_mixes(1.0, 0.1, 2.0, 5000, 1) == {"call": 1}          # same settings file: cached
        os.utime(ex.FIT, (before.st_atime, before.st_mtime + 60))

        os.utime(ex.FIT, (before.st_atime, before.st_mtime))

def _cap(u):
    return min(U_CAP, max(-U_CAP, u))


def _simulate(g, days, steps, chartists, N, v1, v2, a1, a2, a3, s, R, tc, gamma,
              beta, sigma_mu, sigma_eps, tick, floor, n_plus, n_minus, max_gap, max_days,
              hard_gap, cb1, cb2, cb3, halt_steps, pause_end, shock):
    """The simulation loop (see SPEC.md). Returns per-day log price, log value,
    chartist share and opinion at each day's close, the circuit-breaker level of
    each day, and the number of days completed (fewer than `days` if the price ran
    away: |log price - log value| above max_gap for max_days days in a row, or ever
    above hard_gap).
    Circuit breakers: 0 > cb1 > cb2 > cb3 are log falls from the previous close
    (-inf = off). Falling to cb1 or cb2 within the first pause_end steps of the day

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the president's party (extension)
# politics.py and Figs 12-15 found: US stocks returned more under Democratic presidents, but the gap
# is about what luck gives (the real returns with the party calendar slid along), and crashes,
# volatility and fat tails show no party difference. The site shows that test for any market, and
# can add an optional party drift to the model's value (off by default; the paper has none).
PARTY_CALENDAR = "Dow Jones"     # the longest party calendar we have (trading days since 1896)
PARTY_MAX = 0.20                 # largest party drift the site allows: 20 points a year


def party_view(r):
    """The president's-party test for one market's daily log returns r (a Series indexed by date):
    {gap_year (D minus R, log return a year: 0.05 = 5 points), dem_year, rep_year, vol_ratio (D / R),
    kurtosis (D minus R), crashes (crash days per 1,000, D minus R), luck {measure: percentile among
    the shifted calendars, 0-100}, calendars (how many), changes (party changes), dem_days,
    rep_days, start, end}. Days before the first president in politics.PRESIDENTS are left out.
    Raises ValueError when there are fewer than 500 days under either party."""
    if not isinstance(r, pd.Series) or not isinstance(r.index, pd.DatetimeIndex):
        raise ValueError("need daily returns as a Series indexed by dates")
    r = r[r.index >= pd.Timestamp(politics.PRESIDENTS[0][0])].dropna()
    dem = politics.democrat(r.index)
    if dem.sum() < 500 or (~dem).sum() < 500:
        raise ValueError(f"needs at least 500 days under each party (has {int(dem.sum()):,} under "
                         f"Democrats and {int((~dem).sum()):,} under Republicans)")
    v = r.values
    real = politics.party_gap(v, dem)
    shifted = politics.shifted_gaps(v, dem)
    luck = {k: experiments.percentile(real[k], [g[k] for g in shifted]) for k in politics.MEASURES}
    return dict(gap_year=politics.return_gap(v, dem),
                dem_year=float(v[dem].mean() * politics.DAYS_PER_YEAR),
                rep_year=float(v[~dem].mean() * politics.DAYS_PER_YEAR),
                vol_ratio=real["vol"], kurtosis=real["kurtosis"], crashes=real["crashes"],
                luck=luck, calendars=len(shifted), changes=len(politics.switches(r.index)[0]) - 1,
                dem_days=int(dem.sum()), rep_days=int((~dem).sum()), start=r.index[0], end=r.index[-1])


def party_terms(dates):
    """Each presidency within these dates (sorted): [{name, party, start, end}], for shading a chart.
    Dates before the first president in the table are skipped."""
    dates = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates)
    dates = dates[dates >= pd.Timestamp(politics.PRESIDENTS[0][0])]
    if len(dates) == 0:
        return []
    return [dict(name=t["name"], party=t["party"], start=t["start"], end=t["end"])
            for t in politics.terms(dates, min_days=1)]


def party_calendar(days):
    """Which of `days` model days had a Democratic president: the model's days are laid on the last
    `days` real trading days of the Dow Jones (PARTY_CALENDAR), as politics.compare does with the
    model. Returns (bool array, those dates)."""
    days = _whole(days, "days", 1)
    dates = saved_prices(PARTY_CALENDAR).index[1:]       # the dates of its daily returns
    if days > len(dates):
        raise ValueError(f"the party calendar has {len(dates):,} trading days; asked for {days:,}")
    dates = dates[-days:]
    return politics.democrat(dates), dates


def party_shocks(days, burn, party):
    """The party drift as model.simulate shocks: on each model day after the burn-in, the true value
    moves by +party/2 a year (spread over the trading days) under a Democratic president and by
    -party/2 under a Republican one, so the value grows `party` a year faster under Democrats (0.05 =
    5 points). The burn-in days get none. party = 0 gives None: the model exactly as in SPEC.md."""
    if not is_number(party) or abs(party) > PARTY_MAX:
        raise ValueError(f"party drift must be a number from -{PARTY_MAX} to {PARTY_MAX} "
                         f"(a fraction a year), got {party!r}")
    if party == 0:
        return None
    dem, _ = party_calendar(days)
    step = party / 2 / politics.DAYS_PER_YEAR
    return {int(burn) + i: math.expm1(step if d else -step) for i, d in enumerate(dem)}


def model_party_gap(r):
    """The yearly D-minus-R return gap of one model history r (after burn-in), cut at the same
    calendar as party_shocks: what a party drift (or luck alone, without one) gives in the model."""
    r = np.asarray(r, dtype=float)
    dem, _ = party_calendar(len(r))
    return politics.return_gap(r, dem)

def party_gap_without(r, name):
    """The yearly D-minus-R return gap of returns r (a Series indexed by date) with one presidency's
    days left out (name as in politics.PRESIDENTS, e.g. "Hoover"; every term with that name)."""
    if not isinstance(r, pd.Series) or not isinstance(r.index, pd.DatetimeIndex):
        raise ValueError("need daily returns as a Series indexed by dates")
    r = r[r.index >= pd.Timestamp(politics.PRESIDENTS[0][0])].dropna()
    spans = [t for t in politics.terms(r.index, min_days=1) if t["name"] == name]
    if not spans:
        raise ValueError(f"no presidency named {name!r} in these dates")
    keep = np.ones(len(r), dtype=bool)
    for t in spans:
        keep[t["a"]:t["b"]] = False
    return politics.return_gap(r.values[keep], politics.democrat(r.index[keep]))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the president's party (extension)
# Spec: party_view reproduces politics.py's test (the numbers in RESULTS.md, Figs 12-15); party_shocks
# moves the value by +party/2 a year on Democratic days and -party/2 on Republican ones, none in the
# burn-in, and nothing at all for party = 0 (the model exactly as in SPEC.md).

def _dated(values, start="2000-01-03"):
    return pd.Series(values, index=pd.bdate_range(start, periods=len(values)))


def test_party_view_reproduces_results_md():
    dow = e.party_view(e.log_returns(e.saved_prices("Dow Jones")))
    assert round(dow["gap_year"], 3) == 0.035 and round(dow["luck"]["mean"]) == 91 and dow["changes"] == 15
    spx = e.party_view(e.log_returns(e.saved_prices("S&P 500")))
    assert round(spx["gap_year"], 3) == 0.053 and round(spx["luck"]["mean"]) == 95
    assert round(spx["vol_ratio"], 2) == 0.86 and round(spx["crashes"], 1) == -1.6   # RESULTS Fig 12 table
    ndx = e.party_view(e.log_returns(e.saved_prices("Nasdaq-100")))
    assert round(ndx["gap_year"], 3) == 0.117 and round(ndx["luck"]["mean"]) == 91


def test_party_view_by_hand():
    # 2000-2016: Bush (R) to 2009-01-20, then Obama (D). Constant +1 bp on D days, -1 bp on R days:
    # the gap is 2 bp a day, 252 days a year
    r = _dated(np.zeros(4300))
    dem = e.politics.democrat(r.index)
    r[dem], r[~dem] = 1e-4, -1e-4
    r += np.random.default_rng(0).normal(0, 1e-3, len(r))     # some spread, so the sd is not zero
    v = e.party_view(r)
    assert v["gap_year"] == pytest.approx(e.politics.return_gap(r.values, dem), abs=1e-12)
    assert v["gap_year"] == pytest.approx(r[dem].mean() * 252 - r[~dem].mean() * 252, abs=1e-12)
    assert v["dem_days"] == int(dem.sum()) and v["dem_days"] + v["rep_days"] == len(r)
    assert v["changes"] == 1 and v["start"] == r.index[0]
    assert set(v["luck"]) == set(e.politics.MEASURES) and all(0 <= p <= 100 for p in v["luck"].values())


def test_party_view_refuses_too_little_history():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="500 days under each party"):
        e.party_view(_dated(np.full(600, 1e-3), start="2010-01-04"))   # all Obama: no Republican days
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Series indexed by dates"):
        e.party_view(np.zeros(5000))


def test_party_terms():
    t = e.party_terms(pd.bdate_range("2016-06-01", "2021-06-01"))
    assert [(x["name"], x["party"]) for x in t] == [("Obama", "D"), ("Trump", "R"), ("Biden", "D")]
    assert t[1]["start"] == pd.Timestamp("2017-01-20") and t[1]["end"] == pd.Timestamp("2021-01-19")
    assert e.party_terms(pd.bdate_range("1880-01-01", "1890-01-01")) == []          # before the table


def test_party_calendar_is_the_end_of_the_dow():
    dem, dates = e.party_calendar(1000)
    dow = e.saved_prices("Dow Jones").index
    assert len(dem) == 1000 and dates[-1] == dow[-1] and dates[0] == dow[-1000]
    assert np.array_equal(dem, e.politics.democrat(dates))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="party calendar has"):
        e.party_calendar(10 ** 6)


def test_party_shocks_by_hand():
    assert e.party_shocks(5000, 1000, 0.0) is None                 # off: the model as in SPEC.md
    sh = e.party_shocks(5000, 1000, 0.05)
    dem, _ = e.party_calendar(5000)
    assert sorted(sh) == list(range(1000, 6000))                    # every day after the burn-in, none before
    step = 0.05 / 2 / 252
    assert all(sh[1000 + i] == pytest.approx(math.expm1(step if d else -step), abs=1e-15)
               for i, d in enumerate(dem))
    logs = np.log1p([sh[1000 + i] for i in range(5000)])
    assert logs[dem].sum() / dem.sum() * 252 - logs[~dem].sum() / (~dem).sum() * 252 == pytest.approx(0.05, abs=1e-12)
    for bad in (0.25, -0.21, float("nan"), "0.05", True):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="party drift"):
            e.party_shocks(5000, 1000, bad)


def test_party_zero_leaves_the_model_unchanged_and_a_drift_moves_the_value():
    p, burn = e.fitted_settings()
    a, _ = e.run_mix(p, "herding", p["a1"], 1000, 7, burn)
    b, _ = e.run_mix(p, "herding", p["a1"], 1000, 7, burn, 0.0)
    assert np.array_equal(a, b)
    # the value's own path: with a drift its daily changes differ from the no-drift run by exactly the shocks
    from herding import model
    q, _ = e.mix_settings(p, "herding", p["a1"])
    plain = model.simulate(q, 1000 + burn, seed=7)
    pushed = model.simulate(q, 1000 + burn, seed=7, shocks=e.party_shocks(1000, burn, 0.1))
    dem, _ = e.party_calendar(1000)
    extra = np.diff(pushed["lf"])[burn:] - np.diff(plain["lf"])[burn:]
    assert np.allclose(extra, np.where(dem, 0.05, -0.05) / 252, atol=1e-12)


def test_model_party_gap_and_without():
    r = np.zeros(2000)
    dem, _ = e.party_calendar(2000)
    r[dem] = 0.001
    assert e.model_party_gap(r) == pytest.approx(0.001 * 252, abs=1e-12)
    dow = e.log_returns(e.saved_prices("Dow Jones"))
    assert round(e.party_gap_without(dow, "Hoover"), 3) == 0.008                # RESULTS.md Figs 13-15
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="no presidency named"):
        e.party_gap_without(dow, "Lincoln")


def test_a_party_drift_differs_from_the_fit():
    p, _ = e.fitted_settings()
    run = {"a1": 1.0, "a2": p["a2"], "v1": p["v1"]}
    assert not e.differs_from_fit(run, p) and not e.differs_from_fit(dict(run, party=0.0), p)
    assert e.differs_from_fit(dict(run, party=3.5), p)

content.text:
I found and fixed two real bugs between the website and the engine, and the president's party is now on the site in both forms you asked for. All 1,418 tests pass and the stress test has 0 failures.

## Bugs between the website and the engine files
I checked every function the pages call against the engine modules: none are missing. Two problems did turn up:

1. **Stale data after a file changes.** The site caches anything it reads from a file, but the cache only notices when the *code* changes, not the file. After a refit, the site would have kept running the model with the **old** settings. Meanwhile `numbers.json` showed the new results, so the pages would disagree with each other. The same applied to data downloads and caption edits. The cache key now includes each file's "last changed" time, so a changed file is read again.
2. **A module missing from the auto-reload list.** The site now uses `herding/calibrate.py` (and, after today's work, `politics.py` and `experiments.py`). They weren't in `app.py`'s reload list, so after a push the live site would have kept old copies. That's the same kind of bug that crashed the live site in November. A new test now fails if the site ever loads a `herding` module that isn't on the list. I checked that it really catches the problem by taking `calibrate` off the list for a moment.

## President's party, added both ways
1. **On the site, with the luck test from your files.**
   - **Test program:** a "President's party" switch under the price chart. It shades Democratic presidencies in gray (blue and red already mean other things on the site) and labels the presidents.
   - **The panel** shows the gap per year, the luck test (how many fake calendars the real gap beats), volatility and crash days. It works for any market, including tickers you type in.
   - **Findings:** a new section with a table for the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, plus conclusions written from the computed numbers.
   - **The numbers match your report exactly:** Dow +3.5% a year (beats 91% of fake calendars), +0.8% without Hoover; S&P 500 +5.3% (95%); Nasdaq-100 +11.7% (91%).
2. **In the model, off by default.**
   - A "Party drift" slider, from −10% to +10% a year, makes the true value grow faster under Democratic presidents.
   - The model's days are laid on the real presidents' calendar: the last trading days of the Dow.
   - I used the model's existing `shocks` option, the one already built for the Fig 11 policy experiments, so the core simulation loop is unchanged.
   - With the drift at 0 the history is identical, bit for bit, to the original model.
   - A 10-point drift comes out as roughly a 6–9 point gap in the model's prices.

The site keeps your report's conclusion: the real gap is about what luck gives, and party shows no link to crashes, volatility or fat tails. With no drift, the herding model's own "party gap" on the same calendar was −2.3% a year for the S&P history shown, which is pure luck.

**Quick quiz:** why does a 10-point drift in the true *value* come out as only about a 6–9 point gap in the *prices*? (Hint: who in the model pulls the price toward the value, and who ignores it?)

Nothing is committed yet. When you're ready, send me a commit message in your own words and I'll commit everything from today.
